targets.title: The architecture of intuition: Fluency and affect determine intuitive judgments of semantic and visual coherence and judgments of grammaticality in artificial grammar learning.
targets.evidence_quote: Building up on basic research ( Topolinski & Strack, 2009a ; Experiment 8) showing that healthy subjects are more likely to judge triads to be coherent that consist of positive as compared to negative words, we expected that this effect would also emerge for depressed patients.
targets.outcome_quote: Results did not reveal any effect of our fluency manipulation, and thus our hypotheses regarding fluency (H2) were not supported. As such, the current study could not replicate previous results that bolstered the fluency model proposed by Topolinski and Strack (2009a , 2009b ).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Fluency comparison fails, while positive-valence comparison agrees. The fluency passage explicitly contrasts prior results. Additional agreement passage: The results further showed that positive (vs. negative) valence triggered coherence judgments (H3a) and that this effect was – in contrast to our hypothesis (H3b) – not moderated by depression.
